title: D&D 2024 Rule Mechanics
targetDescription: an official 2024 rules update or mechanic

items.label: Grappled condition lowers speed to 0
items.feedback: Correct. The Grappled condition sets a creature's speed to 0 and gives disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than the grappler.

items.label: Grappled gives disadvantage to other targets
items.feedback: Correct. A grappled creature now has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone except the creature grappling it.

items.label: Weapon Mastery: Topple requires a Con save
items.feedback: Correct. The Topple mastery forces a Constitution saving throw or the target is knocked prone.

items.label: Weapon Mastery: Vex gives advantage next turn
items.feedback: Correct. Hitting with a Vex weapon grants advantage on your next attack roll against that target before the end of your next turn.

items.label: Monk Focus Points replace Ki Points
items.feedback: Correct. The 2024 Monk uses Focus Points instead of Ki Points to fuel their features.

items.label: Monk Unarmed Strike can use Dex for grapple
items.feedback: Correct. Monks can use Dexterity instead of Strength when setting the DC for their Grapple or Shove attempts.

items.label: Sorcerer Innate Sorcery grants spell DC bonus
items.feedback: Correct. Innate Sorcery gives a +1 bonus to your Sorcerer spell save DC and advantage on Sorcerer spell attack rolls.

items.label: Potions can be drunk as a Bonus Action
items.feedback: Correct. The 2024 rules codify that administering a potion to yourself is a Bonus Action; feeding it to someone else is an Action.

items.label: Surprise gives -5 to Initiative
items.feedback: Incorrect. Surprise no longer affects initiative; it now grants disadvantage on initiative rolls.

items.label: Surprise grants disadvantage on Initiative
items.feedback: Correct. If you are surprised when initiative is rolled, you have disadvantage on the roll.

items.label: Inspiration is lost on a Long Rest
items.feedback: Correct. Heroic Inspiration resets and is lost if unspent when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

items.label: Exhaustion adds a flat -1 per level
items.feedback: Correct. Exhaustion is now a single-track penalty, subtracting its level from d20 rolls and Spell DCs up to level 10.

items.label: Weapon Mastery: Nick allows extra off-hand attack
items.feedback: Correct. Nick lets you make the Light weapon extra attack as part of the Attack action rather than using your Bonus Action.

items.label: Counterspell forces a Con save
items.feedback: Correct. Counterspell now requires the target caster to succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the spell fails and wastes the slot.

items.label: Paladin Divine Smite is a Bonus Action
items.feedback: Correct. Divine Smite is now a specific spell cast as a Bonus Action immediately after hitting a creature.

items.label: Critical hits double all rolled damage dice
items.feedback: Incorrect. While true, this is a legacy 2014 rule carried forward, not a 2024 mechanical revision or unique update.

items.label: Short Rest takes exactly 10 minutes
items.feedback: Incorrect. A Short Rest still requires 1 hour in the 2024 rules rules text.

items.label: Grapple escapes use an Action standard check
items.feedback: Incorrect. Escaping a grapple is now checked via a saving throw (Athletics or Acrobatics) at the end of the grappled creature's turn.

items.label: Weapon Mastery: Grapple forces an item drop
items.feedback: Incorrect. There is no 'Grapple' weapon mastery property. Property options include Sap, Slow, Push, etc.

items.label: Sorcerer Innate Sorcery costs 2 Sorcery Points
items.feedback: Incorrect. Innate Sorcery is a free feature usable twice per long rest, not powered by Sorcery Points.

items.label: Paladin Smite can be used multiple times per turn
items.feedback: Incorrect. Because it requires a Bonus Action, you can only use a Smite spell once per turn.

items.label: Inspiration allows a full d20 reroll
items.feedback: Incorrect. Heroic Inspiration must be spent *before* rolling to grant advantage, it is no longer an after-the-fact reroll.

items.label: Counterspell uses an automatic ability check
items.feedback: Incorrect. The caster standard ability check vs 10 + spell level was replaced with a target Constitution saving throw.

items.label: Exhaustion halves movement speed at level 2
items.feedback: Incorrect. Exhaustion levels subtract from rolls and reduce speed by 5 feet per level; speed is not halved at level 2.

items.label: Weapon Mastery: Vex auto-crits on next hit
items.feedback: Incorrect. Vex only grants advantage on the next attack roll, not an automatic critical hit.

reflectionPrompts: The 2024 rules shift action economy constraints, specifically making Smites and Counterspell interactive via specific action/save types.
Weapon Masteries add distinct tactical choices to weapon properties, separating functional utility like Topple from action-savers like Nick.
Conditions like Grappled and Exhaustion have been simplified to predictable mathematical penalties to speed up tracking at the table.
